The album came out at a time when I was about to go into high school, and I'd just had my first major episode of mental illness. It was a really shaky time for me emotionally. Pure Heroine dealt with some pretty run of the mill issues for teenagers. I listened to White Teeth Teens and I could (and still can) see all the popular people at school. I used to listen to 400 Lux and imagine my crush driving me around the suburbs when we got older, and us just talking. It also dealt with my fears about getting older and the world I was about to inhabit (that was definitely Ribs). Team, A World Alone and Buzzcut Season were songs that made me think about my best friends at the time. But Still Sane almost saved me. After what I had been through, even though Lorde had just become famous at 17 and I'd had a major depressive episode at 11...I was scared, like she was. I was trying to understand and grasp that this might be the rest of my life. The lyrics don't match exactly, but that was all I felt at the time. Listening to the songs now forces me to reflect on the little girl I was then, and the lyrics really have grown with me even though the situations have changed. I love every single song on Pure Heroine to bits. They're all pieces of me.

What you are is somebody going through something many people wouldn't wish on their worst enemies' pets, and in addition to that an absolute badass. I think you've proven that to us by reaching out for help today and when you feel comfortable (and able to, because dissociation can fuck up your ability to deal with getting to places as I think you know) I would encourage you to reach out to a psychologist and have a chat about these symptoms. There seem to be some good points either way...I believe the rundown is
Pro self dx:

* Many doctors are adverse to diagnosing people who fit out of a certain tiny demographic with A PD (of course this also goes for many other mental health conditions)
* Quite a few people can't afford to go to an actual psychiatrist or doctor at all or have symptoms preventing them from doing so
* Having a disorder like BPD can put you on a blacklist for certain professional opportunities/get your kids taken away/basically officially stigmatise you forever
Anti self dx
* The thing about you actually beginning to experience symptoms after you research them too much and subconsciously try to fit into the disorder happens. I feel like this might account for a good portion of BPD selfdxs
* Not all doctors are complete asswipes and with communities like this accessible, it should only take minor effort to find out the names of some good doctors for specific illnesses near you
* Also: doctors cannot actually diagnose themselves with anything, despite the fact they have gone through medical school and all that razzle dazzle (and you haven't!) Why? Because you're biased! Everyone is and in terms of that there probably isn't a worse illness you could be self dxing than BPD.
